Magen Avot u-Misgav Imahot, an alternate egalitarian ḥatimah for the opening blessing of the Amidah

tei:bibl.tei:title: מָגֵן אָבוֹת וּמִשְׂגָּב אִמָּהוֹת
Magen Avot u-Misgav Imahot, an alternate egalitarian ḥatimah for the opening blessing of the Amidah
tei:bibl.tei:author: Jonathan Schachter
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: Following the insight of my ḥavrutah, Jonathan Schachter, I have begun to include the divine epithet “misgav Sarah” (the fortress, stronghold, or castle keep of Sarah) to the ḥatimah blessing of magen avot, the first blessing of the Amidah. As Jonathan explains, “misgav imahot” already has a liturgical precedent in the ‘anenu litany recited at the end of seliḥot. With respect to the egalitarian impulse to honor both our matriarchal and patriarchal ancestors, I deeply appreciated how “misgav imahot” matched poetically with “magen avot” — each describing the security and protection of the divine in that very vulnerable place of standing before their terrifying throne, aspiring to that earnest sincerity Psalms 51 calls “lev nishbar” (a shattered complacency, as Rabbi David Seidenberg translates it).

This is an egalitarian liturgical innovation for the ḥatimah of the first blessing of the Amidah, magen avot, in which the divine is described as the fortress of Sarah. The insight behind this formulation comes via Jonathan Schachter. English translation of magen avot, including the additions for the six matriarchs and misgav Sarah, by Aharon Varady.

tei:note.tei:p: whereas the now common formulations “ezrat Sarah” and “ufokéd Sarah” do not.
